semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every pair of integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient defined by the given q-Pochhammer ratio is actually a nonzero polynomial with integer coefficients in the formal variable q, and its degree is exactly r times (n-r).
quantifier_order: Then the stated polynomiality and degree claim holds

variables.name: q

witness_dependencies: The polynomial is not an unspecified object; it is the explicit q-binomial expression determined by n, r, and q
The degree claim depends on n and r only

statement_nl: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), where (q;q)_m := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i) and (q;q)_0 := 1, is a nonzero polynomial in Z[q] of degree r(n-r).
